answer: Gate registration on live path diversity: each new key answers timed nonces from three independently run beacons. One datacenter yields one timing vector, so a thousand aliases signed with the same quill look near-identical and collapse into a single cluster. Passing means renting genuinely separated hosts and keeping them awake through every re-check, so each fake identity carries a hosting bill plus outlier-flag risk. Honest agents pay milliseconds and forget it. Across a tundra of cheap cloud addresses those vectors stay flat; across real users they carry the pigment of distance.
